items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: And then I went for many years imitating Pee Wee instead of imitating Johnny Don.

ctx.x: Did you get any idea about sitting out and playing your own notes and being more an individualist?

No, I don't think so. I was always a very imitative musician. Later I got away from the New Orleans influence and I came back to Pee Wee Russell. I don't know if you're aware of this, but when I went to New York, this was mainly due to the influence of Mark Groves. And I began to become more interested in Pee Wee Russell, that understated form of playing rather than the extroverted New Orleans style. And then I went for many years imitating Pee Wee instead of imitating Johnny Don. And for a while I was playing…

It seems to me Marty told me that you had changed your approach. Yes. This was after Marty had been in Chicago, went back to New York and heard you there and came back and said that you enjoyed what you were doing. You seemed to be reasonably happy. There wasn't enough work, maybe that was the problem.
